Commit message / docs claim: 'stale-material — you attested and then edited the plan — still blocks, so the gate is not bypassable by editing after signing'
advisory.finding: The change's central retained security guarantee — 'attest, then edit the plan → stale-material still blocks, so the gate is not bypassable by editing after signing' — is not verified end-to-end against the REAL classifier. After removing the provenance layer, compute_validity is now the ONLY producer of a blocking (FLAG) verdict for the edit-after-sign case, yet no test in the changed file drives classify_plan_review_attestation to a stale-material verdict. Only the abstract bucket partition (stale-material ∈ FLAG_VERDICTS) is asserted; a regression that mis-shapes the `shaped` payload or mis-wires the compute_validity call so it no longer yields stale-material through this gate would pass all changed tests.
scenarios: A future refactor of the `shaped` dict keys (e.g. renaming material_fingerprint) silently breaks stale-material detection; the gate would accept an edited-after-signed plan and the changed tests stay green

dropped.finding: The new classifier reads bound fields from the decoded op-cert PAYLOAD but never verifies the DSSE signature (shaped sets verified=True unconditionally; opcert_from_record only decodes). Comments and the docstring assert the fields are 'read from the SIGNED payload, so a lying plaintext mirror buys nothing' — true for mirror-vs-payload confusion, but the payload itself is no longer authenticated, so a fabricated envelope (any/garbage signature) with a plan-review predicate bound to this ticket now reaches `certified`.
scenarios: An actor able to write the auto-pushed, non-Gerrit-gated tickets branch fabricates a plan-review attestation record; the gate accepts it, removing the only coaching block (LLM-Review/Verified votes remain bot-only).
